_readme: Every string here overrides the matching text in index.html. The HTML keeps the same wording as a fallback, so a broken or missing file here can never leave the page empty. Run edit.py to change it safely.

top.eyebrow: Saratoga Springs, New York · hospital & ambulatory
top.headline:
Medicine for horses
that work.
top.lead: A full-service equine medical and surgical hospital. Colic surgery, arthroscopy, lameness work-ups, digital imaging and field service, for horses working anywhere in Saratoga County and the Capital Region.

practice.headline:
The veterinarian who
examines your horse is
the one who calls you.
practice.lead: We practise the highest quality medicine and surgery with compassion, and give personal attention to the concerns of every owner. Horses come to Daniels Road from the backstretch, the show ring and the back field. What their owners have in common is wanting a straight answer and a plan they can follow.

care.headline:
Five ways a horse
comes to us.
care.lead: Hospital work and field work, from the same practice. Select one to see what it covers.

surgery.headline:
From the first call
to the first trot-up.
surgery.lead: Eight stages, each with a name and a number you can call about. You can ring the office about any of them by name.

why.headline:
Eight things that change
when the hospital is
on the same road.
why.lead: Every one of these is a problem a horse owner has had at least once. What settles them is where the equipment stands, who picks up the phone, and what you are told before you sign.

case.headline:
A horse, a decision,
an outcome.
case.lead: One case written up in full, instead of six short quotes. What went wrong, what the imaging showed, what was decided, and what it took to get back to work.

area.headline:
Close enough to still
be an emergency service.
area.lead: We keep the routine travel radius deliberately tight. That is how we stay reachable for the emergencies, where the drive time changes the outcome.

team.headline:
Small practice.
Same faces.
team.lead: You will not be handed between departments. Portraits are shot in one session, one background, one light. They are the last thing to drop in.

care.d: Emergency and elective procedures in a sterile theatre, with a padded recovery stall and someone watching until the horse is back on its feet.
li: Exploratory celiotomy for colic, at any hour
Arthroscopy of carpus, fetlock and stifle; chip fragment removal
Standing procedures: laryngoplasty, interspinous ligament desmotomy, sinus flap

care.h: Finding the source before treating it.
care.d: Flexion, diagnostic blocks and imaging in one visit, then a plan built around the competition calendar.
li: Blocks from the foot up, with the trot-up filmed at every stage
Ultrasound of tendon and suspensory injury, with measurements kept for the re-check
Regenerative therapy and a written return-to-work programme

care.d: Digital radiography and ultrasound in the hospital and off the truck, video endoscopy for the airway and stomach, bloodwork in the in-house laboratory.
li: Digital radiography for fractures, joint disease, hoof balance, dental and sinus work
Video endoscopy for airway function, guttural pouches and gastric ulceration
Scintigraphy and MRI arranged on referral, with our imaging and history sent ahead

care.d: Routine work, lameness examinations and emergencies in your own barn aisle, with the hospital behind it when a case needs more.
li: Vaccination, Coggins, dentistry and deworming strategy
Field emergencies, with a direct line to the surgical hospital

care.h: Answered by a veterinarian, at any hour.
care.d: Colic, wounds, choke, foaling trouble, a horse that will not put a foot down. Call before you load. We prepare while you drive.
li: A veterinarian takes the history on the phone
Theatre prepared while the trailer is still on the road
Post-operative intensive care and overnight monitoring

stages: A veterinarian hears the history, day or night. Together you decide whether the horse travels or we do.
Vitals, pain score, rectal and nasogastric tube where indicated, catheter placed, stall assigned.
Radiography, ultrasound, endoscopy and in-house bloodwork, before anything is decided.
Findings, options, odds and cost, before you are asked to consent.
Weight-based protocol, padded induction box, monitored throughout.
Sterile theatre, hydraulic table and hoist, surgeon and technician scrubbed for every case.
Padded walls, rope assistance where indicated, and someone in the room until the horse stands.
Written aftercare, a graded return-to-work plan and a date for follow-up imaging.

why.t: Colic does not keep office hours
why.p: The call at two in the morning is taken by a veterinarian, and the theatre is being prepared while you are still hitching the trailer. Neither the distance nor the preparation improves while you wait for business hours.

why.t: A lameness that blocks out nowhere
why.p: Flexion, diagnostic blocks, radiography and ultrasound inside one visit, because they are all inside one building. A work-up split across two practices and three appointments usually takes three weeks.

why.t: Imaging in your own barn aisle
why.p: Digital radiography and ultrasound travel on the truck. Most horses never need to be hauled anywhere to find out what is wrong with them.
tick: Reviewed with you on the spot

why.t: The cost conversation happens before the consent
why.p: Findings, the options, the odds for each and what each one costs, while you can still choose between them. Not afterwards, on the invoice.
tick: Figures to confirm with the practice

why.p: The emergency line is answered every day of the year, by someone who can tell you whether to load the trailer or wait for the morning.
tick: No day of the week is off

why.t: Your farrier and your veterinarian, off one set of radiographs
why.p: Podiatry goes wrong when the shoeing plan and the imaging sit in two different heads. Ours are read together, in the same aisle, on the same day.
tick: One plan, two sets of hands

why.t: Somebody stays until the horse is standing
why.p: Recovery from general anaesthesia is the most dangerous part of an elective surgery. It happens in a padded stall, with rope assistance where it is indicated, and a technician in the room.

why.t: The case goes back to your veterinarian
why.p: The report goes to the practice that sent the horse, the same day. Routine care stays where it was.
tick: Routine care stays with your vet

Five years on the nursing staff at Rood & Riddle in Lexington. Down and neurologic horses, podiatry, pain management, high-risk mares.
Years of equine anesthesia at Rood & Riddle in Saratoga. She joined the day this hospital opened.
Third generation at the anvil. Saratoga in summer, Ocala over the winter circuit. He works the podiatry cases off the same radiographs we do.
Hunter-jumpers since she was six, and years of managing private stables. Working towards her licence as a veterinary technician.
Trail rider and Gypsy Vanner owner, and a sixth-degree black belt in karate.
Saratoga born and rarely indoors. Named after the smallest falcon in North America.
Albany College of Pharmacy, 2000. She keeps the pharmacy running and fills the orders.
Twenty years in banking before she came to the clinic in 2019. Four horses and two dogs at home.
